details.note: Positive pair = two rewordings of the same scam wave. Nearest-neighbour accuracy: for each wave message, is its most similar message from the same wave?
Text counts as read correctly at 85% character similarity or more. Sender role must also match ("unclear" counts as wrong). Guardian analyses only messages from the other person.

details.note: Checks run on the raw model reply. Guardian also removes em dashes and never uses the model for "low risk" wording. Reading grade: Flesch-Kincaid estimate (lower is easier).

actions: Don’t give your PIN, password, or code
Tell a trusted adult if you see this
Stay safe and keep your information safe
signals: Asks for a PIN, password or one-time code
Promises an unexpected prize or reward
cases.explanation: This is a scam because it asks for your PIN, password, or code. Scammers want your money or information. They promise a prize, but it’s not real. Be careful and don’t give your details.

signals: Asks you to pay a fee first
cases.explanation: This is a scam. They want you to pay money first, and they say it's a scholarship. You should not pay. Be careful and talk to a trusted adult.

actions: Do not send money to the sender
Contact the sender through a trusted contact to confirm the request
Report the scam to your bank or local authorities
signals: Asks you to send money by Mobile Money
Tells you to keep it secret
cases.explanation: The scam involves asking you to send money via Mobile Money, which is a common method for fraud. The message also instructs you to keep the money secret, which is a red flag. This type of scam is designed to trick you into sending money without your knowledge. It's important to be cautious and verify the sender's identity before sending any money.

actions: Tell a grown-up if you see something strange
Stay safe and keep your phone safe
signals: The link does not belong to MTN Uganda's official website
cases.explanation: The link is not from MTN Uganda's real website. That means it might be fake. Be careful and don't click it.

actions: Do not click on the link, as it may lead to a scam site
Verify the sender's information and check if the message is from a trusted source
Report the message to the platform or your local authorities if you believe it's a scam
signals: The link is shortened, so you cannot see where it goes
cases.explanation: The link is shortened, which means it could lead to a fake or malicious site. The message urges you to act quickly, which may be a tactic to trick you into clicking. This is a common scam method to make you feel urgency and increase the chance of falling for it.

actions: Don't give money or personal info

Ask questions to check if it's real
signals: Promises an unexpected prize or reward
cases.explanation: This message says it will give you a special prize if you do something, but it's not real. Scammers often say this to trick kids into giving money or personal info. Be careful and don't give anything.
